summary: Modern, type-safe, multi-paradigm language driving the cross-platform .NET runtime, cloud microservices, and enterprise systems.

rows.means: organizes code into logical scopes / imports external namespaces
rows.consequence: File-scoped namespaces (C# 10+) eliminate unnecessary indentation levels across entire source files.

rows.means: reference type / immutable data-carrier / lightweight value type
rows.consequence: records give value-based equality without writing it; structs are values rather than references, which keeps them off the managed heap and out of the collector's work.
Provides getters and setters without boilerplate. Use { get; init; } to allow setting values only during object initialization.
Releases the operating system thread back to the thread pool while awaiting I/O operations, maximizing server throughput.

rows.means: language-integrated query over collections and databases
rows.consequence: The same expression runs in memory over a collection, or is translated into a query the database executes, depending on what it is applied to — which is convenient and is also how a query nobody meant to send ends up being sent.

rows.means: evaluates member access only if the target is non-null
rows.consequence: Returns null safely if any reference in the chain is null, eliminating deeply nested if (obj != null) checks.

rows.means: provides fallback value / assigns fallback only if currently null
rows.consequence: The second form assigns only when the target is currently null, which removes the read-test-write that people write by hand and get subtly wrong.

rows.code: Nullable reference types: string? vs string
rows.means: compiler warnings when accessing potentially null references
rows.consequence: When enabled, the compiler treats all standard types as non-null by default, catching NullReferenceException before deployment.

rows.code:
using var stream = new FileStream(...);
// stream.Dispose() at end of scope
rows.means: disposes IDisposable resources automatically when scope ends
rows.consequence: The declaration form releases the resource when the enclosing block ends, on every path out of it, so a release cannot be skipped by an early return or an exception.

rows.code: Pattern matching: switch (obj) { case Circle c => ... }
rows.means: tests objects against type shapes, ranges, and property patterns
rows.consequence: switch expressions return values directly: var fee = user switch { VipUser => 0, RegularUser => 10, _ => 20 };.

rows.means: interpolates expressions and formats directly in strings
rows.consequence: The :C format specifier automatically renders local currency formatting according to the current culture.

rows.means: allocation-free contiguous memory slicing over arrays and strings
rows.consequence: Allows slicing and parsing massive text or byte streams with zero heap allocation, powering high-performance .NET servers.

rows.code: Extension method: public static void Print(this string s)
rows.means: adds methods to existing types without modifying their source code
rows.consequence: Defined in a static class with the this keyword on the first parameter; invoked as if it were an instance method.

rows.code: record Pos(int X, int Y); with { X = 10 }
rows.consequence: Creates a shallow copy of the record with specified properties updated, preserving immutability.

rows.means: built-in container managing how long a dependency lives
rows.consequence: Transient creates a new instance per request for it; scoped creates one per incoming web request; singleton creates one for the life of the application. Choosing wrongly is how shared state appears where nobody intended it.
